pk.context: 160 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: white to off-white, oblong soft gelatin capsule

clues.kinetics: A high-fat meal has no clinically meaningful effect on exposure. It is 97% to 98% bound to plasma proteins, and hepatic metabolism is its main elimination route.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 464.44. The crystalline solid is non-hygroscopic and practically insoluble in water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 40 mg capsules, and as 40 mg and 80 mg tablets. Taken once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning, and no contraindications. Musculoskeletal pain and fatigue are the most common reactions, at 10% or more.
clues.indication: Castration-resistant prostate cancer, metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, and non-metastatic castration-sensitive cancer with high-risk biochemical recurrence.
clues.mechanism: Competitively blocks androgen binding to the androgen receptor, which stops its nuclear translocation and its interaction with DNA.

tell: Its major metabolite, N-desmethyl enzalutamide, has similar in vitro activity to the parent drug.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: The median T max is 1 hour (0.5 to 3 hours) following a single 160 mg dose of capsules
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The mean terminal half-life (t 1/2 ) for enzalutamide after a single oral dose is 5.8 days
evidence.pill: XTANDI 40 mg capsules are white to off-white oblong soft gelatin capsules
clues.kinetics: There was no clinically meaningful effect on enzalutamide or N-desmethyl enzalutamide pharmacokinetics following the administration of XTANDI with a high-fat meal
Enzalutamide is 97% to 98% bound to plasma proteins, primarily albumin
Enzalutamide is primarily eliminated by hepatic metabolism
clues.substance: Enzalutamide is a white crystalline non-hygroscopic solid
It is practically insoluble in water
clues.safety: the most common adverse reactions (≥ 10%) that occurred more frequently (≥ 2% over placebo) in the XTANDI-treated patients were musculoskeletal pain, fatigue
clues.indication: non-metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (nmCSPC) with biochemical recurrence at high risk for metastasis (high-risk BCR)
clues.mechanism: Enzalutamide has been shown to competitively inhibit androgen binding to androgen receptors; and consequently, inhibits nuclear translocation of androgen receptors and their interaction with DNA
